summary: Both round-5 fairness regressions are fixed, and I confirmed each one in the rendered film.mp4 as well as on the sheets. (1) ch15-s10: the CREDITS card footer says 'Claude is made by Anthropic, a lab in this story, held to the same sources as every other.' from +8.58 to +20.08, above the Strudel line. credits.json footer is an array carrying it. (2) ch14-s04b: HELPS HUAWEI · HUANG (NVIDIA), SELF-DEFEATING · CHINA'S FOREIGN MINISTRY and DECISIVE · AMODEI (ANTHROPIC), KHAN (EX-NSC) hang as one row at equal size and ink. In a frame pulled from film.mp4 at +7.0 (1853.25 s), all three are at full ink. DECISIVE was half-faded at +6.83 and settled by +7.79, and it no longer gets a solo beat in the silent tail. I re-ran the fact machine checks on the 2168.4167 s clock. 234 lines; timeline matchesScript and fresh both PASS. Every shot claim id exists in claims.json. Every quoted span in the narration and in onScreenText is verbatim in quotes.json (the one non-match is the voice name 'Dave Edge' in the credits). Every curly-quoted literal in the shot sources resolves to quotes.json. Every contested claim (29 uses) is shown as contested. I read the new and rewritten lines against the research. L1502 now reads 'He wrote that nobody he met remembered his Versailles talk', which is faithful to q-hopfield-versailles. It credits the Boltzmann machine Hinton co-invented, matching the ch05-s03 card 'with Sejnowski & Ackley', and the medallion tags HOPFIELD NET · 1982 and BOLTZMANN MACHINE · 1983–85 match e4-hopfield and the bible. L1504b matches e14-biology ('suppressing it yields habit'), and ch15-s03 credits it on screen as 'Anthropic, on Claude 3.5 Haiku · via a simplified replacement model' under MARCH 2025. The VTT carries both lines on the new clock (00:32:06.792, 00:32:52.752). In ch15-s05, frame 2003.55 of film.mp4 shows four plates under one light: GOOGLE DEEPMIND / ANTHROPIC / OPENAI / META. 'as of October 2026' appears once, the Lin and Katsas quotes are verbatim to q14-judge-lin and q14-katsas, and 'APPROVED JULY 2026' matches e14-copyright (final approval 20 July 2026). The facts are now clean and the lab and geopolitics framing is even. What is left is small: a human sign-off on name pronunciation (sixth round open), two ledger partials that are really fixed, a source line on the METR ruler that is too small and partly covered, and a stale spec flag on the W8 Hassabis slip.

issues.problem: This is the sixth round with no human sign-off on how the narrator says real people's names. QA narration.listening still marks Uszkoreit, Amodei, Hochreiter, Schmidhuber, Rumelhart, LeCun and Lenat as pending. STT round-trips pass (the new L1502 take hears Hinton and Hopfield literally), but a transcriber matching a spelling is not a listener hearing respect.
issues.fix: Human hand-off before publish (unchanged). Listen to L1006, L1206, L0614, L0507, L0821 (with L0601, L0609 and L1311) and L1104 (with L0515 and L1316) via `npm run film:voice -- listen --slug neural-net-history`. Record each with `film:voice signoff --term <term> --by <name> --verdict ok|reject`. A rejection becomes a solo retake with a lexicon respelling. This does not block the gate.

In round5-shots, ch15-s03 is 'partial' because shotledger's note check pulled the anchors the note REQUIRES ('L1504b', 'Snuff', 'habit') into removedKeys and then failed the shot for containing them. ch13-s03 is 'partial' only on a sha change after recording. issues.fix: Record round5-shots ch15-s03 and ch13-s03 as fixed (closedBy round6), citing ch15-s03 sheet times +11.83 / +14.29 / +17.87 and ch13-s03 +7.83 / +8.87. In generator/film/lib/shotledger.mjs, never treat a quoted token as a removed key when the same note names it as an anchor target (T.word('<line>','<word>') or 'Anchor ... on'). Only phrases after 'remove', 'delete', 'drop' or 'no longer' count. Add a test using the round-5 ch15-s03 note text.

issues.problem: The provenance line under the capability ruler is too small, and a candle covers part of it. The large 'METR, Mar 2025 · doubles ≈ every 7 months' card fades out at about +13.8, just as the '16 HOURS · MAY 2026' rung and 'UNRELIABLE ABOVE HERE' land. From there the only attribution for the top rung is 'METR estimates · frontier models' at about 16 px under MINUTES (film frame 1994.9 s = +13.94), and the shelf candle at x≈950 crosses 'METR'. The 2026 rung, the film's biggest present-day number, is the one whose source a viewer cannot read.
issues.fix: Set 'METR estimates · frontier models' at the film's ≥22 px cap, lift it or move it right so no candle or plate overlaps it from b3 (+8.0) to the cut to the stopwatches (~+14.1). Alternatively, keep the 'METR, Mar 2025 · doubles ≈ every 7 months' card at full ink until the stopwatch cut. Do not name the measured model or lab. Re-sheet at +10.1, +13.9 and +14.1.

issues.problem: Spec hygiene, the same pattern that brought back removed text three times. sets/studyState.ts line 353 still says the W8 slip { who: 'HASSABIS · 2025', text: 'AGI in 5 to 10 years · about even odds', pinned: 'ch15-s06' }, but round 4 removed the pin from ch15-s06 and round 5 removed it from the spec. The slip is sourced (e14-hassabis: 'next five to 10 years', 'maybe a 50 percent chance'), and it may stay on the Wall at rest alpha: it shows in ch15-s09 at +0.92 and +2.75. But a 'pinned: ch15-s06' tag invites a future author to re-animate the pin there.
issues.fix: In studyState.ts, set the W8 slip to on the Wall from the start (drop pinned: 'ch15-s06', or set it to the earliest shot whose Wall shows it), with a comment: 'rest alpha only; never pinned, captioned, pushed or lit (round-4 historian)'. Keep the text exactly as it is. No re-sheet is needed unless the Wall's first appearance changes.

Candle spans: logic machine 1943-59 = 16; sterile extension 1969-86 = 17; hand-cut stencils 1999-2012 = 13; Cyc 1984-2023 = 39, the longest.

L1205: InstructGPT 1.3B over GPT-3 175B, 'despite having 100x fewer parameters' (e11-instructgpt).

The film's own maker gets no extra beat, and the burnt-out 'China is a year or two behind' candle carries its own dates.

ch15-s03 and ch15-s08: Anthropic's interpretability result is shown precisely (Claude 3.5 Haiku, a simplified replacement model, 'one of many such studies'). Then its own limit ('satisfying insight for about a quarter of the prompts') sits beside Jain & Wallace's 'Attention is not Explanation'.
